newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Medco to bid for stake in Burma field.
newsitem.headline: Medco to bid for stake in Burma field.

text.p: Indonesia's Medco Energi Corp said on Wednesday it planned to make a bid to buy Texaco Inc's 42.9 percent stake in Burma's Yetagun gas field.
"Yes, we will make a bid for the Texaco stake in Burma," Arifin Panigoro, Medco's president commissioner, told reporters.
Texaco chief executive Peter Bijur said at the company's annual shareholders meeting on May 13 that it would consider selling the stake in the gas field.
Texaco has the largest stake in and is the operator of the Yetagun gas field. U.S. companies have been under pressure to withdraw investment from Burma because of Rangoon's poor human rights record.
Earlier this year, Washington imposed sanctions to protest what it called political repression by the ruling military junta, banning fresh investment in Burma by U.S. companies.
The Yetagun field is 125 miles off Burma's western coast in the Indian Ocean and is currently being commercially evaluated.
Malaysian national oil firm Petronas has also said it is studying the purchase of the Texaco stake.
